patch.objective: Common attack classes (injection, XSS, buffer overflow) at a conceptual level
secondaryObjectives: Defense-in-depth as a design principle, not a slogan

sources.cite: ACM/IEEE-CS/AAAI, Computer Science Curricula 2023 (CS2023), knowledge areas (SEC: Security)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of the report's first part: 17 knowledge areas, among them SEC: Security. The fetch reached the table of contents, not the knowledge units' topic lists, so topic detail is from the MSCS course's own dated unit sources (read 2026-11-11, REQ-245). The case's decision: recognize blind SQL injection from the request pattern, stop it, ship a parameterized query (data never parsed as code), and limit the database login.

sources.cite: EC-Council, CEH Exam Blueprint v5.0 (CEH v13), Domain 5: Web Application Hacking
sources.note: Read in full as text on 2026-11-14 for REQ-273. Sub-domain 'SQL Injection': SQL Injection Concepts; Types of SQL Injection; SQL Injection Methodology; SQL Injection Tools; Evasion Techniques; SQL Injection Countermeasures. Domain 5 weight 14% (18 of 125 questions).

sources.cite: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series, SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.note: Read 2026-11-14 through a summarizing fetch. Relevant text: primary defenses are 'parameterized queries when including dynamic data in SQL requests' and mapping structural choices to 'a strict allow-list of fixed, application-owned values'; manual escaping is strongly discouraged; least privilege: never give application accounts DBA or admin rights, and grant access through views; 'Input validation complements parameter binding; it does not replace it.'
